title: Ramp cadence signal keeper and KPI playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical, lightweight playbook for running a ramp/cadence-driven launch at Redwood. It stitches together a compact KPI tracker, pre-launch checklist, canary gating logic, and short-run escalation patterns. Intended audience: product-ops leads, release engineers, SRE on-call, and the product launch owner.

Quick context + constraints:
- Goal: Open beta -> 100k monthly active users over 90 days while preserving 99th P95 latency and keeping unit cost within budget.
- Primary signals: latency, error-rate, cost-per-1k-tokens, activation conversion, retention-1d, retention-7d, and quality regressions from eval probes.
- Nonfunctional constraints: Dedicated SLA for enterprise customers must not be impacted; canary traffic kept to isolated pool.

KPI tracker (single-sheet summary):
- Metric: P95 infer latency (prod endpoint) | Target: <= 350ms | Measure cadence: 5m rolling | Owner: eng-release
- Metric: 5xx rate (per-route) | Target: < 0.05% | Measure cadence: 5m rolling | Owner: eng-sre
- Metric: Cost per 1k tokens (hosted) | Target: <$0.12 | Measure cadence: daily | Owner: finance-ops
- Metric: Activation conversion (signup->first API call) | Target: >= 35% | Measure cadence: daily | Owner: product-growth
- Metric: Eval regression rate (golden prompt suite) | Target: 0% new regressions | Measure cadence: per-deploy | Owner: applied-ml
- Metric: Canary user satisfaction (NPS sample) | Target: >= +20 | Measure cadence: weekly survey | Owner: customer-success

Gating logic (canary -> ramp):
1) Canary (1% of traffic to new model or config): must pass 24h window with: P95 within 10% of baseline, 5xx <= baseline+0.01%, and no eval regressions.
2) Ramp to 10%: 48h window, cost delta monitored (alert if > +20%), retention-1d within -5% of baseline.
3) Ramp to 50%: 72h window, SLOs maintained, and user qualitative signals (support tickets) normal.
4) Full rollout: automated if all signals green for 7 days, manual signoff required for enterprise routes.

Pre-launch checklist (owner tags included):
- [eng-release] Canary environment created and route isolation confirmed (IDs: canary-r1, canary-r2).
- [eng-sre] Alerting thresholds and runbook pages updated (link to incident runbook).
- [product-ops] Beta cohort segmented and invites scheduled.
- [privacy] Data residency and KMS checks completed for private customers impacted by rollout.
- [applied-ml] Golden prompt eval set run against production baseline and new candidate (attach results csv).
- [customer-success] Support playbook and canned responses prepared for top-5 expected issues.
- [finance-ops] Cost alarms set and billing path validated for burst traffic.
- [devexp] SDKs pinned to compatible runtime versions, and migration notes drafted.

Escalation matrix (short):
- Tier 1: Ownered by eng-sre on-call — first 15 minutes: triage, rollback decision within 60 minutes if user impact.
- Tier 2: Eng-release + product-ops — coordinate mitigation, run targeted rollbacks or route split within 2 hours.
- Tier 3: Exec brief (VP-level) if major SLA breach affecting enterprise customers or sustained P95 > 2x baseline for >6 hours.

Quick troubleshooting cookbook (notes-to-self style):
- If P95 spikes but 50th median is stable: look at tail behaviors (KV cache misses, long tails due to cold workers). Check batch sizes and worker saturation metrics.
- If error-rate increases only on certain routes: examine model gating config and input length distribution, check for unhandled exceptions in post-processing.
- If cost-per-1k-tokens jumps: inspect batching telemetry and quantization profile usage; consider temporary throttle or color-route low-priority teams to cheaper variant.

Rollout experiments (small, trackable tests):
- Alpha: split traffic by user-agent to isolate SDK beta users for rapid feedback.
- Beta: stagger by region (US-East -> US-West -> EU) to watch regional infra differences.
- Pricing experiment: enable token discount for first 10k tokens to measure acceleration of activation conversion.

Reporting cadence + artifacts:
- Daily digest (automated): P95, 5xx, cost-per-1k, activation conversion — distributed at 09:00 PT to stakeholders.
- Weekly synthesis: trend analysis + top incidents, flagged regressions, and decision memo for next ramp tranche.
- Post-mortem: for any rollback, 48h readout + 7-day corrective action plan.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Do we want automated rollback on eval regressions or manual hold? (current default: manual hold for model-quality regressions).
- Canary size for enterprise tenants: do we route a subset of enterprise accounts or keep them entirely out until full rollout?

Notes / quick links:
- Confluence: Ramp Cadence Charter (linked above).
- Jira: PRODOPS-482 for rollout orchestration board.
- GitHub: launch-scripts PR #77 contains the infra automation for canary routing.

Appendix (short templates):
- Canary signoff template: "Duration, Metrics observed (P50/P95/99, 5xx, cost delta), Eval results summary, Support tickets count, Recommend ramp to X%? [yes/no], Signoff owner and timestamp".

- Post-deploy blurb (to share in #product-launch): "Deployment: <version>, Canary window: 2025-01-15 10:00-2025-01-16 10:00 PT, Current status: Observing (P95 +5% vs baseline), Actions: increase logging, hold for 24h. Owner: Ava Martinez".

This doc is a working checklist — when used in a live launch, drop in real numbers from the automation dashboard, attach the eval csvs, and convert the KPI tracker into the central product-ops sheet. TODO: align final signoff language with legal for enterprise freezes.

-- Ava
